account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill inspection, lunch at home, and now council letters at the office. At the mill I found 82 hay bales in the sales chest, but no one gave me a substantive grain-condition report. I have just asked the secretary for the results of the enquiries and any correspondence requiring a decision; I have not yet heard the answer.

The unusual matter is a repeatedly circulating report about a bridge or port change near the bakery. Several mill townsfolk repeated it, and one said the baker and freight had been there. This does not establish what was said, whether either person proposed anything, or whether there is any actual project. The neighbour had previously heard only a vague version, and the secretary reported no firsthand proposal evidence from either the neighbour or freight. I do not yet know what any supposed change would be for.

The secretary has been trying to locate the town accounts ledger and the normal deposit point for council correspondence. Earlier office searches found appointment records but no proposal, ledger, or correspondence location. My treasury inspection found 128 emeralds and no letters or ledger. Those limited searches do not prove that documents do not exist elsewhere.

There is also a confirmed community gathering with the innkeeper at eighteen hundred in the great hall. I approved it yesterday, and freight has offered an escort from my office, which I authorized the secretary to confirm. That is an ordinary scheduled gathering as far as I know; I have no evidence linking it or the escort to the bridge rumour. I still have tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred, office hours at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen.
